idiom_name: dlopen/dlsym + a shared-object entry symbol returning a function table
implementation_notes: C has no reflection and no runtime type information, so the classic structure is hand-written: the plugin is a shared object that exports one well-known symbol (for example a function returning a const, versioned vtable of function pointers plus an opaque state pointer), and the host calls dlopen with RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL, resolves the entry symbol with dlsym and calls dlclose on unload. Apache httpd is the canonical large-scale realization - each module exports a module record with a magic cookie, a directive table and a hook-registration function, and LoadModule names the symbol to look for - and PAM, GStreamer and NSS follow the same shape. What replaces the named participants is the struct-plus-symbol convention: the vtable is the Plugin Contract, the exported entry point is the factory, and a host-side table of loaded handles is the registry; the classic form stays justified whenever you must add code to a running native process, because the loader is all the runtime offers.
pitfalls: dlsym returns NULL both for a missing symbol and for a symbol whose value is NULL; clear dlerror() before the call and check it afterwards, as the dlopen manual prescribes.

A plugin that registered callbacks or function pointers with the host must be fully drained before dlclose, or the host keeps calling into unmapped code; the reference count means the object stays mapped until every dlopen has been matched.

Without -fvisibility=hidden and RTLD_LOCAL, plugin symbols enter the global namespace and can interpose host or other-plugin symbols; RTLD_GLOBAL is only needed when plugins must resolve each other's symbols.
Library constructors run once per load and global state is not reinitialized by a later dlopen, so a reloaded plugin can observe stale process-wide state.
